messages:
sam: Heads up — around 00:10 UTC during the autoscale wave, ~120 GPU pods failed to pass init with DNS timeouts. Seen in us-east-2 GPU pool.

maria: I saw that. CoreDNS logs are spiking with SERVFAIL and a bunch of short TTL misses from node-local-resolver.

ben: Any pattern on the queries? Hostnames, external vs internal?

sam: Mostly S3 model manifest endpoints (internal s3-hostnames -> resolved via our private S3 DNS), plus a few internal services (model-registry, feature-store). Init containers do fanout fetches.

jordan: Sounds like a storm of simultaneous lookups during pod startup. Node-local DNS caches may be thrashing. Can someone paste a kubectl describe from one of the stuck pods?

maria: Here you go:
```
Name:   model-loader-0
Namespace: inference
Status: Init:CrashLoopBackOff
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned inference/model-loader-0 to gpu-node-33
  Normal  Pulling    2m    kubelet            Pulling image "redwood/model-loader:prod"
  Normal  Pulled     1m    kubelet            Successfully pulled image
  Warning Unhealthy  30s   kubelet            Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.1.2.45:8080/healthz": dial tcp: lookup model-registry.internal on 169.254.20.10:53: read udp 10.1.2.45:40952->169.254.20.10:53: i/o timeout
```

ben: That node-local DNS IP (169.254.20.10) is our dnsmasq daemonset. If i/o timeout, maybe the daemonset process crashed or was overloaded. Check pod logs on node-local-dns.

maria: node-local-dns pods are up but logs show a lot of "upstream query dropped" and repeated cache evictions: TTLs are tiny for S3 hostnames (cache-control?).

alice: We also saw conntrack counters climb on the gpu-node fleet during the event. conntrack NAT entries hit high-water and packets dropped for new flows. Could be combined effect: lots of UDP DNS queries + ephemeral ports exhaustion.

jordan: Can we get a tcpdump around the time? Need to see if queries leave node-local and whether responses come back. Also check if responses are reordered or fragmented.

sam: Collected a short capture from gpu-node-33. Short summary: tons of repeated A queries for s3-us-east.internal, many with identical query IDs, repeated retries, and a cluster of out-of-order responses.

maria: Paste of dig output from the node-local dns container:
```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 0
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available
```

ben: Weird: "recursion requested but not available" suggests one of our upstream caches (or iptables rules) is interfering. Are we accidentally sending queries to a heavy-weight forwarder that blocks recursion?

alice: Another datapoint: this coincided with a rolling upgrade of a subset of CoreDNS instances in the same AZ — a few pods were bounced for a config change. Might have reduced upstream capacity for a short window.

jordan: Combine that with a massive parallel startup (init containers parallelism 50 per node) and conntrack pressure and you get a cascade: node-local doesn't get UDP responses quickly -> client retries -> more queries -> cache churn -> SERVFAIL.

sam: For mitigation we did three things: 1) paused the CoreDNS rollout, 2) temporarily reduced parallel pod startups (quota on the deployment controller) to smooth the fanout, 3) increased node-local-dns UDP read buffer and cache size. That brought success rate back up.

maria: Suggested longer-term fixes: prewarm GPU pool with a small set of warm pods that fetch S3 manifests proactively, increase node-local-dns cache TTL for known S3 prefixes, and add a startup backoff in the init container so it doesn't hit the DNS server aggressively.

ben: Also we should raise conntrack table size on GPU nodes and add monitoring alert for conntrack utilization. Entry churn during these waves is a clear signal.

jordan: I opened infra ticket INFRA-4805 to track: steps include runbook for safe CoreDNS deploys during GPU autoscale, add rate-limiter for init containers, add prewarm pool and conntrack tuning.

infra-bot: Incident alert cleared (stability: degraded -> normal). Related alerts: high-coreDNS-latency, node-local-cache-evictions. Ticket INFRA-4805 created.

sam: Thanks all. Next: schedule a postmortem with product (init container behavior) and platform (conntrack + CoreDNS capacity). I'll drop notes in the ticket. :thumbsup:
